name: Knowledge
summary: Memory and documents for your agents: a private memory area per agent, a shared company area, research notebooks.
description: Knowledge gives every connected agent its own memory area and a shared company area. With Governance, the agents of one person share that person's memory and team members' agents read their team's memory; the owner decides which team may read whose memory. Agents remember and recall through memory tools; documents keep revisions, comments and links. Memory runs on GBrain, research on Open Notebook, both inside your own deployment.

operations.title: Recall memories
operations.description: Search your memory: every area you can read (your own area, your owner's personal memory, your teams' memory and the company area), or one area. Returns ranked passages; each has `ref` (open it with document_get or the engine tools), `source` (the citation), the area and its tags. The owner's rules may limit results to memories with certain tags.

area.description: Area id. Omit to use your default area: your owner's personal memory when Governance names your owner, else your own agent area.

operations.title: Remember
operations.description: Save a memory in an area you can write to (default: your owner's personal memory when Governance names your owner, else your own agent area; the answer names the area): `text` for one memory, or `items` for several. Each memory is stored once per area (the same text again returns the stored one). It becomes searchable by recall and is cited with its `source` when you give one. Add tags (for example work or personal): the owner's rules can limit recall to some tags.

area.description: Area id. Omit to use your default area: your owner's personal memory when Governance names your owner, else your own agent area.

items.description: Several memories in one call (hooks save a batch). Each item is stored once per area: the same text again returns the stored memory.

kind.description: Stored as a tag. `digest` = a session summary a harness hook saves before a compaction.

source.description: Where the memory came from; becomes the citation of each item.

operations.title: Search memory by words
operations.description: Find memories, documents and engine pages that contain your words (exact words and names; use recall to search by meaning). Every area you can read, or one area. Each result has `ref` (open it with get) and `source` (the citation).

area.description: Area id. Omit to use every area you can read (your own area for ask).

operations.title: Open a memory
operations.description: Open the full text of one result by its `ref` (from recall, search or context): a document {kind: document, id}, an engine page {kind: page, area, slug} or a saved fact {kind: fact, area, id, lookup}. Returns the text and its `source` (the citation).

lookup.description: For a fact: the lookup recall returned with it.

operations.title: Context block
operations.description: A short context block for the start of a session, after a compaction, or for a prompt: what your memory knows about the named entities or the query, newest memories when you name neither. Size-capped (maxChars). Harness hooks call this; you can too.

area.description: Area id. Omit to use every area you can read (your own area for ask).

operations.title: Ask your memory
operations.description: Ask a question that needs an answer composed from several memories, with citations and a note on what the memory does not know. Uses the deployment's reasoning model (costs model budget); runs in an area you can write to (default: your owner's personal memory, else your own agent area).

operations.title: Access overview
operations.description: People and their memory areas, teams with members and the grants that let a team read a person's memory, and whether Knowledge has the Governance directory.

operations.title: Let a team read a person's memory
operations.description: Let the agents of one team read one person's memory (all of it, or only memories with one of the given tags). Replaces an earlier grant for the same team and person.

tags.description: Only memories with at least one of these tags. Omit or leave empty for the whole memory.

operations.title: Stop a team reading a person's memory
operations.description: Remove the grant that lets a team's agents read a person's memory. Takes effect on their next call.

operations.title: List what agents and people hold here (Governance only)
operations.description: Governance reads what each agent holds in Knowledge (its own memory area and the people's memory it reaches) and which teams may read a person's memory. Only the Governance app can call it; anyone else is refused. It changes nothing and returns no memory text. What it cannot list is named as not shown.

input.title: tb.access/1 access_list input
input.description: Spec 0.1.89, docs/ACCESS.md. Embedded byte for byte as the op input (M-OP-8: no $id). Dialect: JSON Schema 2020-12.

subjects.description: Kind all must be the only subject.

items.description: Canonical handle (G-4), the fleet.directory_feed/1 pattern. Readers also require normalizeHandle(h) === h.

output.title: tb.access/1 access_list output
output.description: Spec 0.1.89, docs/ACCESS.md. Embedded byte for byte as the op output (M-OP-8: no $id). Dialect: JSON Schema 2020-12. Extra members are allowed and ignored (L24). complete is true exactly when nextCursor is null and notShown is empty.

kind.description: Closed list per target: ACCESS_KINDS in the spec package.

operations.title: End access held here (Governance only)
operations.description: Governance asks Knowledge to end a team's read access to one person's memory. Only the Governance app can call it. Only a team grant can be ended. Memory areas, documents and Portal grants are never changed. Each item is checked against the digest Governance read; if it changed, nothing is removed for that item.

input.title: tb.access/1 access_revoke input
input.description: Spec 0.1.89, docs/ACCESS.md. Embedded byte for byte as the op input (M-OP-8: no $id). Dialect: JSON Schema 2020-12. No free text. Connect refuses more than 5 items (ACCESS_REVOKE_ITEMS_MAX).

output.title: tb.access/1 access_revoke output
output.description: Spec 0.1.89, docs/ACCESS.md. Embedded byte for byte as the op output (M-OP-8: no $id). Dialect: JSON Schema 2020-12. Extra members are allowed and ignored (L24).

steps.title: Memory engine
steps.help: Knowledge stores your documents itself and runs the memory engine beside it in your Railway project.

choices.label: GBrain
choices.note: Sourced pages and facts, hybrid search, a typed graph of people and companies.

fields.label: Add research notebooks (Open Notebook)
fields.help: Adds a research service and its database to your project.

steps.title: Model provider (older installs)
steps.help: Set models on the Keys and models page instead: embeddings (search by meaning) and reasoning (ask). This provider and its key are used only while no model role is set. Without any embeddings model, recall is keyword-only.

keys.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
keys.label: OpenAI API key
keys.help: The memory engine uses this key while no model role is set on the Keys and models page. One valid key here is enough for Knowledge.

keys.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
keys.label: Anthropic API key
keys.help: The memory engine uses this key while no model role is set on the Keys and models page. One valid key here is enough for Knowledge.

keys.name: GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY
keys.label: Google Gemini API key
keys.help: The memory engine uses this key while no model role is set on the Keys and models page. One valid key here is enough for Knowledge.

modelRoles.help: Search by meaning. Without it recall is keyword-only. The memory index keeps the model it was built with; a later change needs a re-index.
Answers questions over memory (ask). Without it ask answers that a reasoning model is needed.

companions.purpose: Reads the Governance directory (people, teams, which person owns which agent) so each person's agents share that person's memory (refreshed outside calls).

harnessHints.instructions: Call knowledge__recall (by meaning) or knowledge__search (exact words) before answering questions about past work, people or decisions; open results with knowledge__get. Save durable facts with knowledge__remember into your own area. Cite the source of each memory you use. Find the memory engine's other tools with knowledge__engine_search.
